posts.title: DC Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: My problem with the theory that the secret character in the set is a character in Man of Tomorrow who they are keeping secret is that as soon as this set is unveiled it’s going to spoil that character being in the film, which I can’t imagine WB and DC are going to be ok with a spoiler like that coming out. Especially since this set releases in July, it’s going to be unveiled before Man of Tomorrow comes out. Now, granted, this problem isn’t quite as bad if the set is comic based as they can always chalk it up to the sets creators including a character just because they like them. But Lego knows at this point that leaks are going to happen and labeling the character as a mystery is only going to draw more attention to that character once the set is unveiled. Not to mention DC and WB know by now that telling you companies about secret characters in films is the easiest way to leak them. If there is a secret character in MoT, there’s a very good chance Lego has no idea who it is. IMO, and I will be the first to admit I am probably very wrong on this, but it would make more sense to me that this is another Daily Bugle type situation where not all the characters are included in the artwork the leakers got their hands on. So the mystery character isn’t necessarily a secret character in MoT which WB and DC likely wouldn’t want Lego or any other toy manufacturer even knowing about. Instead, it’s probably just someone the leakers couldn’t identity or there was something ominous like “and more” which indicated there are more minifigures the leakers didn’t see. Let’s not forget, the leak did say “mystery character(s)” not “mystery character,” which lends credence to the idea that the leakers don’t know how many minifigures are in the set or the full list of characters. As for the rumors, my guess is that the leakers heard they’re in the set but aren’t confident enough to say it yet or are just keeping to themselves for some other unknown reason. And honestly, their inclusion would make sense given they have a history together in the comics and I’m sure their inclusion would be a pretty big selling point. IMO, their inclusion might actually be a stronger indication this is a comic based set (and we don’t have another Fantastic Four situation on our hands) and that there may be hope for a few other characters who aren’t in the DCU to make an appearance.

posts.title: [MOC] Mechatech 6x6 All Terrain Tow Truck (42070 10th Year Anniversary Model)
posts.text: And i forgot to, post these pictures. Here is the model with bullbar removed:). Here is shot for the rear axle suspension:). The rear axles uses linkages when other axle is up the other axle goes down. This is my first moc which uses this and this helps with the balance:). Behind the scenes stuff:). Developement pictures:). Ok, i normally dont use old and retired pieces. But this model is my first which uses old and retired pieces. The turntable is from 42006 and this model is not compatible with the new and current 2015 Arocs turntable design. When i started this project my vision was to control 4 functions with 2 gearboxes. But i soon runned out for availdable space. So i made only one gearbox which drives the 2 functions and all the other functions are operated separately. When i created the Mechatech Snow Cat i wasn't happy how the boom looked it was just too bulky and the connection to the chassis looked pretty rough. So i redesigned the boom from scratch for this model and luckily this boom doesn't look bulky. This model's outriggers are my most complex outriggers yet. If you are curious why in the instructions the test for the outriggers comes so late. Is because the side panes lock then so they won't detatch from the build during testing and if you have to adjust them it is pretty simple job. The front and rear outriggers operate at different speeds to make them operate synchronized. The drivetrain for the gearbox i designed pretty much firstly and it was always next to the engine and the shaft in display mode acts as an exchaust pipe and when you start playing with this model. You just connect the gear to the exchaust pipe and start playing:). The engine was firstly planned to be upright. But since the engine room did have little room i had to place the engine flat so it would fit:). And since this model is 1612 and really dense. This model is really heavy. But really strong. Since i do design my models with strict standards and durability in mind for rough playing:). This model the third model which uses my redesigned front axle for the unimog. Im really impressed how strong my designed front axle was and how reusable it was. This model probably is the heaviest which uses this type front axle:). I wish you to have a massive fun time building and playing with the Mechatech 6x6 All Terrain Tow Truck:).
